members.name: token
members.param: Cancels the call, together with the cancellation token set on the underlying command: either one cancels it, whether it is opening the connection, looking up stored-procedure parameter names, executing or reading.

members.name: buffer-token
members.param: Cancels the read: a consumer then sees the cancel after what was already delivered.

members.name: buffered
members.para: All rows are buffered in memory before the call returns. Use to process very large results as a stream.

members.name: handler-result
members.typeparam: The type returned by the handler.

members.name: handler-sync
members.param: Receives a forward-only sequence of mapped rows. Enumerate it inside the handler; it is not valid after the handler returns.

members.name: handler-items
members.param: Receives a forward-only asynchronous sequence of mapped rows. Enumerate it inside the handler; it is not valid after the handler returns.

members.name: handler-async
members.param: Receives a forward-only asynchronous sequence of mapped rows and the cancellation token in effect. Enumerate it inside the handler; the sequence and the token are not valid after the handler returns.

members.name: returns-task
members.returns: A task that completes after the handler has completed and the connection has been released.

members.name: returns-task-result
members.returns: A task that produces the value returned by after the connection has been released.

members.name: null-row
members.para: A row whose value is NULL is still a row, and is returned for it.

members.name: no-rows
members.para: The no-rows error is thrown after the command has been cleaned up: the connection is released and, unless was called, the later result sets have been read through, so a failure in one of them is thrown instead.

members.name: terminal-through
members.para: Called through , the types of this library behave exactly as their own members do, including how the later result sets are read through. Another implementation of is read through its Read handler: it stops at the row, so it cannot read through the later result sets.

members.name: terminal-through-throwing
members.para: Called through , the types of this library behave exactly as their own members do, including the no-rows message and how the later result sets are read through. Another implementation of is read through its Read handler: it stops at the row, so it cannot read through the later result sets, and its no-rows error is the message of LINQ, which does not name the terminal.
